claim: Swamped canoe at the design load (118 kg net) floats with 113 mm freeboard amidships, 92 mm at the lowest point, with the water inside level with the lake (the USCG swamped condition)
law: Archimedes: lift of the foam and timber below the waterline equals the net weight; water inside the flooded hull carries nothing while it flows freely in and out (33 CFR 183.220(g))

claim: Straight after swamping, with the hull brim-full and the water trapped above the lake level, the canoe still floats (24 mm freeboard) and rises as the crew bail
law: Reserve at zero freeboard 277 kg over the outer waterplane 11.4 m2 (trapped water rises with the hull, level canoe); a sealed hull drains only over the gunwale, so this is the state until the crew bail (see S32 to S34)

claim: Swamped roll stiffness 761 kg m per radian, metacentric height 3.1 m
law: Lost-buoyancy method (water inside flowing freely): K = rho I_T + B z_B - W z_G; hand estimate: rho I_T of the foam strips and planks only. The 3.1 m is K over the net weight carried, not a metacentric height of the whole displacement
check: claimed 761 kg m/rad, estimate 783 kg m/rad (ratio 0.97)

claim: The same foam laid on the floor gives no roll stiffness with 5 kg more load, so the modules must sit high (roll stiffness of the floor arrangement)
law: Foam fully under water leaves only the planks' waterplane; K = rho I_T + B z_B - W z_G

claim: All four crew holding one grab line heel the swamped canoe 3.9 deg (limit 10)
law: Heel = heeling moment / roll stiffness (small angles)

claim: With the largest module lost and 5 % uptake the canoe still floats (25 mm lowest freeboard)
law: Archimedes with one 1,400 mm module removed and foam lift down 5 %

claim: Lowest freeboard stays at or above 50 mm with the design net load 20 % higher and foam lift 5 % lower
law: Re-solve of the LVH-CAL-001 equilibrium with both inputs at their pessimistic values

claim: Closed-cell polyethylene foam loses under 5 % of its lift to water uptake after 30 days immersed
law: Closed-cell PE foam sheet, 33 kg/m3: water absorption under 2 % by volume after 28 days (EN 12087), Ravago Ethafoam data sheet; lift lost = absorbed volume x 1,000 / net lift of 970 kg/m3
closed_by: Cited data sheet; immersion test at TRL 4 (R6)

claim: Polyethylene foam is not dissolved by petrol, diesel or fish slime (polystyrene is excluded for that reason)
law: Polymer solubility: polyethylene dissolves only in hot aromatic or chlorinated solvents (above about 80 C); at ambient low-density PE swells and softens a little in petrol; polystyrene dissolves
check: The foam is about 3 % polymer by volume, so swelling does not change its lift; softening and diesel and fish-slime exposure are covered by the cover and the R6 immersion test at TRL 4

claim: PVC-coated tarpaulin covers and polyester webbing keep their strength for 12 months in tropical sun and water
law: UV photo-degradation of PVC coatings and polyester fibres; UV-stabilised grades are sold for outdoor use, but strength retention after a year in equatorial sun depends on the grade
check: Cannot be shown by calculation; strap and cover inspection in field use (R9, TRL 4 and later)

claim: Each M8 coach screw carries twice its share of the full lift (0.30 kN): at twice the load 0.60 kN, of which 0.51 kN along the frame face and 0.32 kN pulling the batten off it (static; wave slam not included)
law: Interaction (F_ax / R_ax)^2 + (F_v / R_v)^2 <= 1 at twice the load; R_v 1.5 kN (LVH-CAL-001 A9, conservative against a Johansen estimate of about 5 kN), R_ax 8.0 kN from the EN 1995-1-1 withdrawal expression for screws, 600 kg/m3 hardwood, 48 mm penetration

claim: Webbing and D-ring buckles carry twice the full lift of the largest module (lowest factor, D-rings)
law: Load per strap = full lift / 2; parts specified at 10 kN webbing and 4 kN D-ring pair (BOM lines 8, 9, to confirm with real parts)

claim: End chock screws (5 x 60 mm) bite far enough into the batten: 31 mm (was 10 mm when driven straight down through the 50 mm chock)
law: Pointside penetration of at least 6 d (30 mm for a 5 mm screw), EN 1995-1-1 practice for laterally loaded nails and screws; screws now driven parallel to the frame face in 12 mm counterbores 30 mm deep; margin 1.3 mm, so the counterbore depth is a making check (LVH-DWG-103)
closed_by: LVH-DEC-001 D-S1 (was Fails, fix proposed: 10 mm)

claim: Coach screws go 48 mm into the frames and stop 12 mm short of the planking (no new hole below the waterline)
law: Penetration at least 6 d = 48 mm (EN 1995-1-1 practice); frame moulded depth 60 mm; planking untouched; no margin either way, so each frame's depth is measured and the screw length chosen to suit (LVH-DEC-001, to confirm item 2)

claim: Grab-line eye bolt (M8 x 100) passes through strake, plank, two washers and a nyloc nut with thread to spare (2.9 mm)
law: Grip at 625 mm: strake and top plank; ISO 7089 washers 1.6 mm, ISO 7040 nut 9.2 mm; at least one 1.25 mm pitch beyond the nut

claim: A crew member holding on with head and shoulders out puts about 15 kg (20 % of 75 kg) on the canoe
law: Body segment masses (Winter): head and neck 8.1 %, forearms and hands on the gunwale about 5 %; the body below the water is close to neutral

claim: 4 crew bail at 100 L per minute each (1.17 m3 in about 3 min)
law: Lifting work is small (about 11 W against 75 W sustained); the limit is the cycle: 100 L/min is about 14 scoops a minute for many minutes; sustained rates of 30 to 50 L/min are more usual (independent review)
check: Rate to measure in the bail-out trial (R4, TRL 4); see S34

claim: Partly bailed to 200 mm freeboard with all crew aboard and 2.3 m3 of water still inside, the canoe keeps a positive metacentric height (0.14 m after the free-surface loss)
law: GM = KB + I_T / V - KG - i_fs / V: KB 0.25 m, waterplane I_T 1.38 m4, free surface i_fs 0.98 m4 of a 1.19 m wide pool, KG 0.22 m with crew seated (CG 0.68 m)

claim: The only new hull holes (eye bolts, 625 mm up) stay above the loaded waterline of the dry canoe (175 mm)
law: Dry displacement 1068 kg (timber at 750 kg/m3, crew, motor, fuel, gear, catch, kit) on the model hull

claim: Modules take 8.4 % of the inside volume below the gunwale
law: 0.421 m3 of module envelope over 5.01 m3 inside volume

claim: Kit mass 70 kg per canoe
law: Sum of stock quantities in the BOM times densities

claim: Stainless kit hardware does not corrode the fixings away in wet hardwood in fresh or salt water
law: All metal in contact is A4 stainless (screws, D-rings, eye bolts): no galvanic couple. A4 can suffer crevice corrosion in wet, salty, airless timber, so screws are inspected at each refit; zinc coatings are attacked by tannins in fresh water too, so the BOM's hot-dip galvanised alternative is withdrawn in favour of A4 (LVH-DEC-001 D-S2)

claim: Fungal decay does not start at the new screw holes in the frames within the kit's life
law: Wood-decay fungi need timber moisture above about 20 %; frames of a working canoe are wet, so the holes are sealed with preservative or epoxy (BOM line 14) and inspected
check: Depends on timber and care; inspection at each refit

claim: A builder and a helper fit the kit in about 6.7 h
law: Bottom-up count by the author (not independent): 20 marks, 8 battens, 20 screws, 16 counterbored chocks, 16 straps, 8 eye bolts, marks; sealer cure not included

claim: Lowest freeboard stays at or above 50 mm if the wet hull timber is denser than water, 1,100 kg/m3 (75 mm; 57 mm at 1,200 kg/m3)
law: Saturated hardwood can exceed 1,000 kg/m3, so A2 is neutral, not conservative; re-solve at 1,100 and 1,200 kg/m3; the real hull is weighed before fitting (LVH-DEC-001, to confirm item 3)

claim: R2 as restated for the free-flooding condition: the lowest point keeps 50 mm with the water inside at the lake level; brim-full, a sealed hull still floats and the crew bail at once, seated
law: Brim-full freeboard (S2) less the trim drop to the lowest point of LVH-CAL-001 (21 mm)
check: 24 mm level, about 3 mm at the lowest point brim-full; R2 is met once the water inside is down to the lake level (by bailing or by water spilling out as the canoe rolls). Amish decided on 2026-10-25 to keep the hull sealed and state R2 and R3 for the free-flooding condition of the USCG method, with the operating rule "hold on, then bail at once, seated"; freeing ports studied at TRL 4 (LVH-DEC-001 D-O2)

claim: The swamped canoe floats level (R3) whether or not the water inside can flow in and out
law: Sealed hull, water trapped: K = rho (I_out - i_fs) + B z_B - W z_G; brim-full: I_out 2.14 m4, free surface 2.01 m4; at the lake level: I_out 1.73 m4, free surface 0.46 m4 between the modules
check: Roll stiffness about 70 kg m/rad brim-full (near neutral; the estimate of the centre of weight is good to about +-200) and 1213 kg m/rad once the water inside is down to the lake level, where the modules cut its free surface. Brim-full, the canoe lolls a degree or two until the low gunwale dips and water spills out, which lowers the inside level and stiffens it; to confirm in the swamp test of a sealed hull (R3, TRL 4)

claim: The four crew, each with a bailer, bail the brim-full canoe to 200 mm freeboard within 15 min (R4) at a sustained 50 L/min each
law: Brim-full water 4.47 m3 less the 2.31 m3 that may stay aboard
check: 2.16 m3 at 4 x 50 L/min takes about 11 min (two bailers took about 22 min). Four bailers decided by Amish on 2026-10-25 (LVH-DEC-001 D-O3); rate to measure in the bail-out trial

claim: Option B: swamped canoe on external sponsons floats with 158 mm lowest freeboard
law: Same equilibrium as LVH-CAL-001 with the foam outside the planks, 360 to 560 mm up

claim: Option B: the new bolt holes through the planks (325 mm up) and the sponson bottoms (360 mm) stay above the loaded dry waterline
law: Dry loaded draft on the model hull, as S19. The holes are below the swamped waterline, so they must be bedded watertight or they leak while the canoe is bailed

claim: Option B: sponsons survive beaching, rafting alongside other canoes and wave slap
law: External fenders and sponsons on working boats wear and tear at the chine and ends; the tarpaulin cover is the only skin
check: Abrasion life to establish in field use

claim: Option C: swamped canoe hung between two pipe floats has 160 mm lowest freeboard
law: Same equilibrium with two 250 mm floats 2.1 m off the centreline; booms and struts counted as weight

claim: Option C: each boom carries half the full lift of one float pushed under by a wave (2.15 kN) at 1280 mm from the gunwale bolts: 8.5 MPa
law: Cantilever, sigma = M / Z, Z = b d^2 / 6 (the boom is continuous across the canoe, so the gunwale bolts take the uplift of the couple, about M / 1.64 m); hardwood of strength class D30, 30 MPa characteristic, design value about 30 x 0.7 / 1.3 = 16 MPa (EN 338, EN 1995-1-1 modification and material factors)

claim: Option C: the SDR 26 float pipe does not collapse when pushed 0.5 m under (3.0 m of water collapse head)
law: Ring buckling of an unsupported pipe p_c = 2 E / (1 - nu^2) (t / (D - t))^3, long-term E of PE100 about 200 MPa, nu 0.4
check: 3.03 m of water >= 0.5 m of water
